headline: Litton backs Tigers to win tri-series despite recent batting struggles
summary: Newly appointed ODI captain Litton Das expressed optimism about Bangladesh's chances in the upcoming tri-nation series against Zimbabwe and Afghanistan, emphasizing the need for good cricket.
details: Newly appointed ODI captain Litton Das has voiced confidence in Bangladesh's ability to win the upcoming tri-nation series against Zimbabwe and Afghanistan. He stated, "If we play good cricket, why not?", during a pre-match press conference.

Litton's optimism comes amidst recent batting struggles for the Tigers, particularly against these two opponents. Both Zimbabwe and Afghanistan have had the upper hand in recent ODI series against Bangladesh.

Bangladesh suffered a 3-0 whitewash against Afghanistan in Abu Dhabi in October 2025, the same venue for the upcoming series opener against Zimbabwe. They also lost 2-1 to hosts Zimbabwe in July this year.
However, under previous captain Mehidy Hasan Miraz, the Tigers showcased strong home form, securing four consecutive series wins against West Indies, Pakistan, New Zealand, and Australia.

Away from home, the batting unit has consistently struggled. During the Zimbabwe tour in Harare, Bangladesh failed to chase a modest 141, folding for 116, and were skittled for 234 chasing 247 in the second match.

The Afghanistan series was even more challenging, with Bangladesh failing to bat out their full 50 overs in any match. They were bowled out for 109 and 93 in the final two ODIs, losing the last by 200 runs.

Litton stressed the importance of senior players taking responsibility. He highlighted the team's inability to bat out 50 overs, a recurring issue against Afghanistan and Zimbabwe, calling for collective effort.

He also noted the team's limited options, often playing with only six specialist batters. This puts extra pressure on the batting unit if the lower order cannot contribute sufficiently, impacting chases of big targets.

Litton himself has faced scrutiny for inconsistent white-ball form, though his ODI numbers in 2026 show improvement with 300 runs in nine innings at an average of 42.86. This follows a difficult 2024 and 2025.

Despite batting depth on paper with players like Tanzid Tamim, Soumya Sarkar, Najmul Hossain Shanto, Towhid Hridoy, and Litton, consistency remains a challenge. The bowling unit, however, is considered a strength.

Zimbabwe is also recovering from a 3-0 loss to Australia last month, though they pushed the world champions to the brink in one match. This offers Bangladesh an opportunity, but success is not guaranteed.

headline_marked: [[Former Additional Secretary dies]] after fall from under-construction building at Officers Club Dhaka
headline: Former Additional Secretary dies after fall from under-construction building at Officers Club Dhaka
summary: Former Additional Secretary Md. Mosharraf Hossain, 72, was found critically injured at Dhaka's Officers Club and later succumbed to his injuries in the hospital. Police suspect he fell from a vacant space in the building's basement.
details: Former Additional Secretary Md. Mosharraf Hossain, 72, was found in a bloody state at an under-construction building inside Dhaka's Officers Club yesterday morning. He was rushed to the hospital but died later that night. Police suspect he fell from a vacant space in Basement-1 to the floor of Basement-3.

According to Ramna Police Station OC Md. Yasin Mia, Hossain went to the Officers Club to teach his younger daughter swimming. He left his daughter near the swimming pool and entered the under-construction building.

Around 11:15 AM, he was found unconscious near a staircase on the ground floor and taken to BARDEM Hospital. He was later transferred to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared him dead around 11:45 PM.

CCTV footage from the Officers Club shows him repeatedly going up and down, possibly looking for a way out, before falling from a vacant space in Basement-1. An inquest report has been prepared for his body.

Family members opted against an autopsy, and the body will be handed over to relatives for burial after his elder daughter, who lives in the US, returns to Bangladesh. Hossain was a member of the Officers Club and resided in Banani, Dhaka.
